chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubaydillah Al-Musi narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Nahik, from Muhammad Al-Farrash, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad Al-Tahhan, from Bashir Al-Dahhan, from Rifah ibn Musa Al-Nahhas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, whoever travels to the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, arrives at the Euphrates, performs Ghusl in it, and steps out of the water, he will be like one who has stepped out of his sins. And when he walks toward the Hā'ir, for every step he takes, Allah will record ten good deeds for him and erase ten bad deeds.

key_terms.الْحَائِرِ: The Hā'ir, a specific area near the shrine of Imam Husayn in Karbala
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ (ع): Imam Husayn, grandson of the Prophet, peace be upon him
key_terms.الْفُرَاتَ: The Euphrates River, a significant geographical and spiritual landmark in Shia tradition

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for performing Ghusl in the Euphrates before visiting Imam Husayn's grave?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), highlighting the Euphrates as a sacred conduit for spiritual purification prior to the Ziyārah of Imam Husayn (a.s.). The narrative underscores the concept of 'Ma'rifah' (gnostic recognition) of the Imam's rights as a prerequisite for the reward, where each step toward the Hā'ir (the dry, sandy plain of Karbala) acts as a mechanism for expiation, granting ten good deeds and erasing ten sins. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical journey mirroring the internal spiritual ascent, linking the geography of Karbala directly to divine mercy.
